n: A taunt-song against Babylon, pictured as a pampered princess who will be pulled off her throne to sit in the dust. Her days of luxury are over. Babylon fell to Cyrus in 539 BC.

f.g: A poetic personification: Babylon as a young, never-conquered princess.
The dynasty ruling Babylon in Nebuchadnezzar’s time.

n: The princess becomes a slave: grinding grain, hitching up her skirt to wade rivers into exile. This is what Babylon had done to captives; now it happens to her.

f.w: Take the millstones, and grind meal
f.g: Grinding grain was the work of the lowest servants and captives.
Remove your veil—a sign of humiliation for a noblewoman.

n: Her shame will be exposed. God will take vengeance and spare no one.

f.w: I will not meet thee as a man
f.g: Possibly “I will spare no one,” or “no one will intercede.”

n: A burst of praise from God’s people: our Redeemer is the Lord of Hosts, the Holy One of Israel. Babylon’s fall is His work.
Babylon must sit silent in darkness—no longer called “queen of kingdoms.”

f.g: Mistress or queen of the nations.

n: God explains: He was angry with Israel and let Babylon conquer them as discipline. But Babylon went too far—showing no mercy, crushing even the elderly with heavy burdens.

f.g: Profaned My own heritage—let My people be treated as common.

f.w: thou didst shew them no mercy

n: Babylon thought she would be queen forever and never considered how it would all end.

f.w: I shall be a lady for ever

n: She lives for pleasure, feels secure, and says, “I am, and there is no one else”—claiming the very words God uses of Himself. She thinks she will never be widowed or lose children.

f.w: I am, and none else beside me

n: Both disasters will strike in a single day—loss of children and widowhood—despite all her sorceries and spells.

f.w: in a moment in one day

n: She trusted her own wickedness and thought, “No one sees me.” Her wisdom and knowledge led her astray. Pride in human cleverness without God leads to ruin.

f.w: Thy wisdom and thy knowledge, it hath perverted thee

n: Disaster will come that she can’t charm away or buy off, and ruin will fall suddenly from where she doesn’t expect.

f.w: thou shalt not know from whence it riseth
f.g: Or “you won’t know how to charm it away.”
Avert it, perhaps by paying a ransom or performing a ritual.

n: A sarcastic challenge: go ahead, keep using all the spells you’ve practiced since your youth—maybe they’ll help!
Babylon was famous for astrology. Isaiah mocks it: let your star-gazers and monthly forecasters stand up and save you. They’ll wear you out but won’t rescue you.

f.g: Those who made predictions at each new moon.

n: They will burn like straw—not a cozy fire to warm yourself by, but a blaze that consumes them.
All the advisers and merchants Babylon relied on will scatter, each going his own way. No one will save her. Revelation 18 reuses this imagery for the spiritual “Babylon” of the last days.
